blocks.prompt: 1 (i) A particle is moving in a straight line and its acceleration is given by \(a = 2t - 7\). Find velocity \(v\) in terms of \(t\) if \(v = 10\) m/sec, when \(t = 0\).
blocks.explanation:
Yeh motion ka sawal hai. Acceleration velocity ke badalne ki raftar hai, yani \(a = \frac{dv}{dt}\).
Diya kya hai? \(a = 2t - 7\) aur shuru mein (\(t = 0\) par) velocity 10 m/sec.
Find kya karna hai? \(v\) ko \(t\) ki shakal mein, yani velocity ka formula.
Rule kaunsa? \(\frac{dv}{dt} = 2t - 7\) ek separable differential equation hai, kyunke right side par sirf \(t\) hai.
Plan: integrate karenge, phir \(v(0) = 10\) se constant nikalenge.
steps:
Diya gaya: \(a = 2t - 7\); \(t = 0\) par \(v = 10\) m/sec.
Maloom karna: \(v\), \(t\) ki shakal mein.
Tareeqa: \(a = \frac{dv}{dt}\) likh kar variables alag karenge, integrate karenge, aur initial condition se constant of integration tay karenge.

Differential equation likhein
\[\dfrac{dv}{dt} = 2t - 7\]
\[dv = (2t - 7)\,dt\]
Kyun: acceleration ka matlab hi hai velocity waqt ke saath kitni tezi se badal rahi hai, yani velocity ka derivative. Phir dono taraf \(dt\) se multiply kiya taa ke \(v\) ek taraf aur \(t\) doosri taraf ho jaye.

Dono taraf integrate karein
\[\int dv = \int (2t - 7)\,dt\]
\[v = t^{2} - 7t + C\]
Kyun: power rule se \(\int 2t\,dt = 2 \cdot \frac{t^{2}}{2} = t^{2}\) aur \(\int 7\,dt = 7t\). Indefinite integral mein constant \(C\) zaroor lagta hai, kyunke kisi bhi constant ka derivative zero hota hai.
Dhyan dein: \(C\) bhool gaye to initial condition lagane ki jagah hi nahi bachegi.

\(v(0) = 10\) lagayein
\[10 = 0 - 0 + C\]
\[C = 10\]
\[v = t^{2} - 7t + 10\]
Kyun: \(t = 0\) rakhne par \(t\) wale saare terms zero ho gaye, is liye \(C\) seedha shuru wali velocity ban gaya.

Tasdeeq
\[\dfrac{d}{dt}(t^{2} - 7t + 10) = 2t - 7 \;\checkmark\]
\(v(0) = 10 \;\checkmark\)
Kyun: derivative lene se wapas wohi acceleration aa gaya, aur shuru ki condition bhi poori ho gayi. Dono baatein sahi hain, to jawab pakka hai.

blocks.prompt: 1 (ii) A particle is moving in a straight line and its acceleration is given by \(a = 2t - 7\). Find distance \(s\) in terms of \(t\) if \(s = 0\) m [printed as 0 m/sec], when \(t = 0\).
blocks.explanation:
Ab distance chahiye. Velocity distance ke badalne ki raftar hai: \(v = \frac{ds}{dt}\).
Diya kya hai? Part (i) se \(v = t^{2} - 7t + 10\), aur \(t = 0\) par \(s = 0\).
Find kya karna hai? \(s\), \(t\) ki shakal mein.
Rule kaunsa? Phir se separable equation; ek dafa aur integrate karna hai.
Plan: \(\frac{ds}{dt} = t^{2} - 7t + 10\) ko integrate karein, phir \(s(0) = 0\) lagayein.
steps:
Diya gaya: \(v = t^{2} - 7t + 10\) (part (i) se); \(t = 0\) par \(s = 0\).
Maloom karna: \(s\), \(t\) ki shakal mein.
Tareeqa: \(v = \frac{ds}{dt}\); variables alag kar ke integrate karenge aur \(s(0) = 0\) se constant nikalenge.

Differential equation likhein
\[\dfrac{ds}{dt} = t^{2} - 7t + 10\]
\[ds = (t^{2} - 7t + 10)\,dt\]
Kyun: velocity distance ka derivative hai. Yaad rakhein: acceleration se velocity ke liye ek integration, velocity se distance ke liye doosri integration.

Dono taraf integrate karein
\[\int ds = \int (t^{2} - 7t + 10)\,dt\]
\[s = \dfrac{t^{3}}{3} - \dfrac{7t^{2}}{2} + 10t + C_2\]
Kyun: har term par power rule \(\int t^{n}\,dt = \frac{t^{n+1}}{n+1}\) lagaya: \(t^{2} \to \frac{t^{3}}{3}\), \(7t \to \frac{7t^{2}}{2}\), \(10 \to 10t\). Naya constant \(C_2\) likha, kyunke yeh part (i) wale \(C\) se alag hai.

\(s(0) = 0\) lagayein
\[0 = 0 - 0 + 0 + C_2\]
\[C_2 = 0\]
\[s = \dfrac{1}{3}t^{3} - \dfrac{7}{2}t^{2} + 10t\]
Kyun: \(t = 0\) par saare \(t\) wale terms zero ho jate hain, is liye \(C_2 = 0\).

Tasdeeq
\[\dfrac{ds}{dt} = t^{2} - 7t + 10 = v \;\checkmark\]
\(s(0) = 0 \;\checkmark\)
Kyun: derivative lene se part (i) wali velocity wapas aa gayi aur shuru ki condition bhi sahi hai.

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Kitab mein doosri condition '\(s = 0\) m/sec, jab \(t = 0\)' chhapi hai. m/sec velocity ki unit hai; distance metre mein naapa jata hai, is liye sahi condition hai: \(t = 0\) par \(s = 0\) m. Hal aur jawab par is ka koi asar nahi.
